results.title: Injection Molding Tariffs are Reinstated | Thogus | Family-Owned High Volume Injection Molding Manufacturer for Ohio and Beyond
results.content:
On July 6, 2018, the U.S. government instituted a 25% tariff on Chinese imports (including tooling used in custom injection molding), igniting concerns among domestic mold builders and manufacturers who had relied on Chinese imports for tooling. The immediate impact of this tariff was short-lived, however, as of December in the same year, Chinese tooling imports were granted a one-year exemption, in part as a result of concern that the tariff would severely disrupt manufacturing supply chains [...] Bottom line: We can expect cost increases throughout the supply chain as a result of the 25% tariff on Chinese imports, and the sourcing of tooling in custom plastic injection molding is likely to be hit hard. Reshoring is one way to get around this new expense, as well as the uncertainty it is causing within plastic injection molding companies currently operating in China.

This measure aims to encourage domestic mold production but has led to increased expenses for companies that previously sourced molds internationally. [...] As of March 2025, the U.S. government has imposed a 25% tariff on imported steel and aluminum, eliminating previous exemptions for countries like Canada, Mexico, and those in the European Union. This policy aims to bolster domestic metal production but has resulted in increased costs for manufacturers reliant on these materials. [...] Like most service providers in the American manufacturing industry, injection molders face potential cost increases due to new tariffs in 2025.

One one hand, raised tariffs are likely to raise the cost of imported products from overseas injection molders. That could potentially be a boon for domestic manufacturers, as their pricing becomes more competitive within the global market.

results.title: Trump Revises Tariffs, Impacting Plastics Industry Imports
results.content: Annex III of the proclamation provides temporary relief for certain plastics machinery, parts, and molds, including specified Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) lines 8477 and 8480. For these products, a combined duty cap of 15% will apply through Dec. 31, 2027. Starting Jan. 1, 2028, Annex III products will transition to standard tariff treatment outlined in the proclamation. [...] The administration has announced a 15% tariff on specific metal-insensitive industrial and electrical grid equipment and a 10% levy on imported goods made entirely of steel, aluminum, or copper from the US, effective through 2027. Section 232 tariffs will no longer apply to goods containing 15% or less of these metals. Initially introduced by Trump, steel and aluminum tariffs were later expanded to include various vehicles, appliances, and household items. Copper imports have faced a 50% duty [...] According to the Plastics Industry Association (PLASTICS), industry members should review imported products classified under HTS 8477, 8480, and related machinery categories to confirm their inclusion in Annex III. For products outside Annex III, businesses should assess whether they fall under the 25% or 50% full-value tariff categories. Evaluating eligibility for reduced US-origin metal treatment and confirming compliance with the 15% metal-weight threshold are also critical steps.
